items.followUp: Write the chemical formula of aluminium oxide and magnesium chloride.

rubric.why: Award for the correct formula of calcium phosphate.
rubric.how: Check that calcium phosphate is written as Ca₃(PO₄)₂.

rubric.why: Award for the correct formula of sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Check that sodium chloride is written as NaCl.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so it is neutral.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that an atom has no net charge.

rubric.why: An ion is charged because an atom has gained or lost electrons.
rubric.description: Ion has a charge due to electron transfer
rubric.how: Look for both the charged nature of an ion and its formation through electron gain or loss.

modelAnswer: An atom is electrically neutral because it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
An ion is a charged particle formed when an atom gains or loses electrons.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of sodium and explain what it shows.

rubric.why: Electronic configuration describes how electrons are arranged or distributed.
rubric.how: Look for the idea of arranging or distributing electrons.

rubric.why: At this level, the arrangement is described as electrons distributed among shells or energy levels.
rubric.description: Electrons in shells or energy levels
rubric.how: Look for shells or energy levels as the locations in which the electrons are arranged.

modelAnswer: Electronic configuration is the arrangement or distribution of an atom’s electrons in its shells (energy levels).

items.followUp: State two limitations of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: The model could not explain why orbiting electrons do not lose energy and fall into the nucleus.
rubric.how: Look for the unexplained stability of the atom or electrons not collapsing into the nucleus.

rubric.why: The model could not explain the line spectra of atoms.
rubric.how: Look for the inability to explain atomic line spectra.

modelAnswer: It could not explain the stability of the atom: revolving electrons should radiate energy and eventually fall into the nucleus.
It could not explain the line spectra of atoms.

items.followUp: Describe the trend in atomic radius across a period and give a reason.

rubric.why: Ionization energy generally increases across a period from left to right.
rubric.how: Look for an increase in ionization energy from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic radius make electrons harder to remove.
rubric.how: Look for increased nuclear attraction or a smaller atomic radius as the reason.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
Nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases, so the outer electrons are held more strongly.

items.followUp: What are a group and a period in the periodic table?

rubric.why: Groups are the vertical columns of the periodic table.
rubric.how: Look for a group identified as a vertical column.

rubric.why: Periods are the horizontal rows of the periodic table.
rubric.how: Look for a period identified as a horizontal row.

modelAnswer: A group is a vertical column in the periodic table.
A period is a horizontal row in the periodic table.

rubric.why: Atomic radius is measured outward from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Look for a distance measured from the nucleus.

rubric.why: The radius extends to the outermost shell or valence shell of the atom.
rubric.how: Look for the outermost or valence shell as the endpoint.

modelAnswer: The atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell of an atom.

items.followUp: Why do atoms lose, gain or share electrons when forming chemical bonds?

rubric.why: Bonding helps atoms achieve a stable outer-shell electron arrangement.
rubric.how: Look for a stable electronic configuration, noble-gas configuration or complete outer shell.

rubric.why: A complete octet or duplet (and thus a more stable, lower-energy state) explains why atoms form bonds.
rubric.how: Look for an octet or duplet, or the resulting stable or lower-energy state.

modelAnswer: Atoms form chemical bonds to attain a stable electronic configuration like that of a noble gas.
They do this by completing an octet or duplet in their outermost shell.
